name: Simulation-based inference and emulators for LSS
summary: Neural emulators replace expensive N-body or Boltzmann runs, and neural density estimators enable likelihood-free inference from galaxy surveys and weak lensing.

name: ML classification of transients
summary: Time-domain surveys such as ZTF and Rubin rely on neural classifiers and anomaly detection to triage millions of alerts and photometrically classify supernovae.

name: N-body simulations as gravitational MD
summary: Cosmological N-body codes use the same symplectic leapfrog integrators and force softening as MD, with tree or particle-mesh gravity in place of Lennard-Jones forces.

name: MCMC for CMB parameter estimation
summary: Metropolis-Hastings sampling, as in CosmoMC, explores the multidimensional CMB likelihood. It made six-parameter ΛCDM fits to Planck tractable.

name: Boltzmann codes for CMB spectra
summary: CAMB and CLASS integrate coupled Einstein–Boltzmann hierarchies for photons, baryons, neutrinos and dark matter. Stiff ODE solvers handle tight coupling before recombination.

name: Hydrodynamic solvers in cosmological simulations
summary: Finite-volume, AMR and SPH schemes evolve gas with gravity in galaxy-formation simulations. Subgrid models for cooling, star formation and feedback supply the physics that is not resolved.

name: Symplectic integrators for orbital dynamics
summary: Wisdom–Holman mapping splits the Hamiltonian into Kepler and perturbation parts. It enabled long-term chaos studies of planetary orbits and the Nice model.

name: Dark matter vs modified gravity as theory choice
summary: The MOND versus particle dark matter debate mirrors Neptune versus Vulcan: anomalies can be absorbed by new matter or new laws. It engages Lakatosian research programmes and underdetermination.
breaks: Unlike Vulcan, the dark-matter hypothesis has independent evidence from the CMB and the Bullet Cluster, and MOND struggles with clusters.

name: Spherical harmonics and Legendre expansion of the CMB
summary: The temperature sky is expanded in spherical harmonics, and the angular power spectrum is the rotation-invariant variance. Statistical isotropy makes the C_ℓ the full description of Gaussian fluctuations.
map: \frac{\delta T}{T}=\sum a_{\ell m}Y_{\ell m},\ C_\ell=\langle|a_{\ell m}|^2\rangle

name: Special functions in galactic potentials
summary: Galactic potentials and Poisson solutions in disk geometry use Bessel functions, Legendre expansions and elliptic integrals. They underpin mass models fitted to Gaia kinematics.

name: Poisson equation and the growth of perturbations
summary: Linear perturbations obey a damped-oscillator-like ODE sourced by the Poisson equation. Green's-function solutions yield growth factors and the transfer function that shapes the matter power spectrum.

name: Stellar structure as a nonlinear boundary-value problem
summary: Hydrostatic equilibrium, mass continuity, energy generation and transport form coupled ODEs with boundary conditions at centre and surface. The Lane–Emden equation is the polytropic special case.

name: FLRW as a maximally symmetric spacetime
summary: The FLRW metric is the warped product of time with a maximally symmetric 3-space of constant curvature k. Friedmann equations follow from the Einstein tensor evaluated on it.

name: Lensing as geodesic deflection in curved spacetime
summary: Null geodesics in a weak-field metric give the deflection angle, and the lens equation maps it to image positions. Shear and convergence are components of the Jacobian of the lens map.

name: TES bolometers and CMB polarimetry
summary: CMB experiments such as ACT, SPT and BICEP use transition-edge-sensor arrays limited by photon and thermal noise, with SQUID multiplexed readout.

name: Cryogenic sensors and low-background detectors
summary: Transition-edge sensors, bolometers and low-noise readout, developed for general detector physics, enable sub-GeV dark-matter searches. Noise floors and background rejection set the reach.

name: Cosmology as statistical inference
summary: Cosmology has a single observable universe, so cosmic variance, MCMC chains, Fisher forecasts and Bayesian evidence are the core tools for extracting parameters and testing models.

name: Bayesian inference of ΛCDM parameters
summary: Cosmological parameters are fitted by Bayesian posterior sampling over likelihoods built from CMB, BAO and supernova data, with priors and model comparison deciding between ΛCDM extensions.

name: Priors, degeneracies and model selection in ΛCDM
summary: Parameter degeneracies (e.g. Ωm–H0, w0–wa) and prior choices shape cosmological constraints. Information criteria and Bayes factors adjudicate extensions such as curvature or dynamical dark energy.

name: Profile likelihood and exclusion limits
summary: Direct-detection limits use profile-likelihood tests, CLs and the Feldman–Cousins construction. Background-dominated searches face the look-elsewhere effect and the neutrino fog.

name: Detection statistics for exoplanet signals
summary: Planet detection uses periodograms, false-alarm probabilities, MCMC orbit fits and Bayesian model comparison for the number of planets. Noise from stellar activity requires Gaussian-process modelling.

name: Systematics budgets in the H0 tension
summary: The H0 tension's significance depends on how statistical and systematic errors, covariances and calibration chains (Cepheids, TRGB) are propagated. Distance-ladder error budgets are an applied GUM-style case.

name: CP violation and the baryon asymmetry
summary: Sakharov's conditions require C and CP violation, baryon-number violation and departure from equilibrium to generate the matter–antimatter asymmetry. The Standard Model's CP violation is far too small.

name: Particle-physics symmetries behind annihilation signals
summary: Annihilation channels and spectra depend on the gauge representation and quantum numbers of the dark-matter candidate, as for a WIMP in SU(2)_L multiplets. These fix branching fractions to gamma rays and antimatter.

name: Broken time translation and energy in an expanding universe
summary: FLRW has no timelike Killing vector, so total energy is not conserved. Radiation redshifts as a⁻⁴ and the cosmological constant does work, though local ∇_μT^{μν}=0 persists.
breaks: Only the global energy notion fails; local covariant conservation holds.

name: Solar oscillations as normal modes
summary: Helioseismic p-modes are standing waves of the solar cavity, described by spherical-harmonic eigenfunctions. Frequencies invert to give the sound-speed profile, as in a spectral problem for an oscillator.
breaks: The Sun is a non-ideal, rotating, convective cavity, so modes are damped and stochastically excited, and rotation splits the degenerate m levels.

name: Inflaton as an order parameter
summary: A scalar field rolling in a potential mirrors the order parameter of a symmetry-breaking transition. The same potential structure underlies Higgs-like phase transitions, topological defects and old/new inflation.
breaks: Inflation requires slow roll on a flat plateau, which is not generic for SSB potentials, and the inflaton has no established particle identity.

name: Homology and mass–luminosity scaling
summary: Dimensional and homology arguments give stellar scalings such as L∝M³ for radiative stars and the Eddington luminosity, together with the Chandrasekhar mass from fundamental constants.

name: Constraints on varying constants from the CMB
summary: A different fine-structure constant or electron mass at recombination shifts the recombination epoch and alters peak positions. Planck data and quasar absorption spectra bound such variation.

name: Cosmological constant problem across Planck scales
summary: Planck-unit estimates of the vacuum energy exceed the observed dark-energy density by about 120 orders of magnitude. The mismatch is the sharpest naturalness problem.

name: Action-angle variables and Delaunay elements
summary: Hamilton–Jacobi theory yields Delaunay and Poincaré action-angle variables, the basis of canonical perturbation theory, averaging and Hamiltonian maps for planetary dynamics.

name: Collisionless Boltzmann equation from Liouville
summary: Liouville's theorem gives the collisionless Boltzmann equation, which underlies Jeans equations and mass estimates from stellar and galaxy dynamics, including rotation curves and velocity dispersions.

name: Phase-space density constraints on halos
summary: Liouville conservation of coarse-grained phase-space density limits how dense a halo core can be, giving Tremaine–Gunn bounds on warm and fermionic dark matter.

name: Symplectic integrators for long-term orbits
summary: Liouville's theorem and symplectic structure motivate Wisdom–Holman integrators that preserve phase-space volume and bound energy error over Gyr integrations.

name: Newtonian cosmology and minisuperspace action
summary: Friedmann equations follow from Newtonian energy conservation of a test shell, and from a minisuperspace Lagrangian in the scale factor.
breaks: Pressure gravitates and k is geometry in GR; the Newtonian derivation lacks this and fails for radiation and dark energy without ad hoc input.

name: Scalar field as particle in a potential
summary: Inflaton dynamics map to a particle rolling in a potential with Hubble friction; slow roll is the overdamped limit.
breaks: Fluctuations are quantum fields on curved space; the point-particle picture misses perturbation generation.

name: Roche potential in mass transfer
summary: The restricted three-body effective potential in a rotating frame defines Roche lobes and the L1 point, governing mass transfer and contact binaries.

name: Fermat's principle in gravitational lensing
summary: Lensing images are stationary points of the time-delay surface (geometric plus Shapiro delay), giving the lens equation and time-delay cosmography.

name: Accretion flows as viscous fluid dynamics
summary: Accretion disks around black holes are viscous shear flows, and Bondi accretion is a spherical ideal-flow solution, as in the Navier–Stokes and Euler problems.
breaks: Angular momentum transport needs MHD turbulence (MRI), not molecular viscosity, and relativity matters near the hole.

name: Shock and blast-wave hydrodynamics
summary: Sedov–Taylor and Blandford–McKee blast waves are self-similar solutions of the Euler equations, applied to GRB afterglows, supernova remnants and the shocks that accelerate cosmic rays.

name: Jeans instability and structure growth
summary: Gravitational collapse of perturbations is the Jeans instability of a self-gravitating fluid, the fluid-mechanics seed of the growth of cosmic structure, modified by expansion drag.
breaks: Dark matter is collisionless, so a fluid description holds only approximately, and nonlinear collapse needs N-body treatment.

name: Convection in stellar interiors
summary: Rayleigh–Bénard-type instability sets the Schwarzschild criterion for convection in stars, handled with mixing-length theory.
breaks: Stellar convection is highly turbulent, compressible and stratified, at huge Rayleigh numbers beyond lab regimes.

name: Dust-gas drag in disks and Stokes drag
summary: Small dust grains in protoplanetary disks couple to gas through Stokes or Epstein drag, setting stopping times and radial drift; the same viscous-drag physics governs low-Re flow.
map: t_s=\frac{m v}{F_{\rm drag}},\; F=6\pi\mu a v
breaks: Disk gas is often rarefied (Epstein regime, mean free path > grain size), unlike continuum Stokes flow.

name: Disk turbulence and angular momentum transport
summary: Turbulent viscosity (alpha prescription) drives accretion in protoplanetary disks and concentrates dust in vortices and eddies, controlling planetesimal formation.

name: Turbulent fragmentation and the IMF
summary: Supersonic turbulence in molecular clouds, with a Kolmogorov-like cascade, shapes the density distribution and fragmentation, and thus the stellar initial mass function.
breaks: Gravity, magnetic fields and feedback also matter; whether turbulence alone sets the IMF is debated.

name: MOND modifies Newtonian dynamics
summary: MOND modifies the Newtonian force law below an acceleration scale, reproducing flat rotation curves and the Tully–Fisher relation without dark matter.
breaks: Fails to account for cluster masses and CMB peaks without extra components, and needs a relativistic completion.

name: Rotation curves from Newtonian orbits
summary: Circular-orbit balance gives velocity profiles; flat curves at large radius imply M(<r) growing linearly with r, which signals dark matter.

name: Kepler orbits and precession in the Solar System
summary: Kepler problem, effective potential and perturbed-orbit precession underlie planetary and small-body orbits; secular perturbations produce apsidal and nodal precession.

name: Cluster collisions and conserved quantities
summary: Merging clusters (e.g. Bullet Cluster) are analysed with momentum and energy conservation and collision kinematics, constraining collisionless dark matter versus shocked gas.

name: Virial theorem and cluster mass
summary: Energy and momentum conservation lead to the virial theorem, used to estimate cluster dynamical masses from galaxy velocity dispersions (Zwicky's missing mass).

name: Planetary systems as few-body problems
summary: Planetary system architecture, stability and resonances are treated with the N-body problem, perturbation theory and numerical integration.

name: Lagrange points and Trojans in exoplanet systems
summary: Restricted three-body equilibria define Trojan configurations and co-orbital planets, searched for in exoplanet timing and transit data.

name: Timing and RV signals from N-body dynamics
summary: Transit-timing variations and radial-velocity multi-planet fits are inverse N-body problems; mean-motion resonances amplify TTVs, allowing masses to be inferred from perturbations.

name: Resonances and N-body Solar System evolution
summary: Mean-motion and secular resonances, symplectic N-body integrators and perturbation theory are the working tools of Solar System dynamics.

name: Coriolis force and atmospheric circulation
summary: Rotating-frame dynamics sets hot-Jupiter and terrestrial jet and wave structure, via Rossby numbers and geostrophic balance.

name: Tides and Coriolis in planetary systems
summary: Tidal forces from non-inertial frame analysis drive tidal locking, orbital migration and Roche limits; Coriolis force shapes planetary atmospheres and rotating-frame Hill dynamics.

name: Chaos in N-body stellar dynamics
summary: Exponential sensitivity in few-body encounters and cluster dynamics limits N-body predictability, so ensembles are used for population synthesis.

name: Orbits and resonances in the Galactic potential
summary: Action-angle methods and resonance structure describe stellar orbits in barred potentials; bar resonances produce moving groups and phase-space features seen in Gaia.

name: KAM tori and chaos in planetary stability
summary: Long-term stability of planetary orbits is a KAM question: resonance overlap produces chaotic zones, Kirkwood gaps and Lyapunov times of order millions of years for the Solar System.

name: Fuzzy dark matter solitons
summary: Ultralight scalar dark matter obeys a Schrödinger–Poisson system whose ground state is a stable soliton core in halos, tied to nonlinear Schrödinger structure.
breaks: Poisson coupling is nonlocal, so the system is not integrable like the cubic NLS and solitons are not exact.

name: Driven damped oscillator and acoustic peaks
summary: Photon-baryon plasma modes obey a forced, damped oscillator equation, with gravity driving, baryon loading shifting the zero point, and Silk damping suppressing high multipoles.
breaks: Damping is from photon diffusion at finite mean free path, not a simple friction term; the system is also relativistic.

name: Normal modes of the Sun
summary: Solar p-modes and g-modes are the normal modes of a stratified self-gravitating sphere, and helioseismology inverts mode frequencies to infer interior structure.

name: Baryon acoustic oscillations as sound waves
summary: BAO are sound waves in the pre-recombination plasma that froze at the drag epoch, leaving a standard ruler equal to the sound horizon.

name: Parametric resonance in preheating
summary: After inflation, the oscillating inflaton drives daughter fields through Mathieu-equation parametric resonance, producing explosive particle production.
breaks: Backreaction and rescattering end the resonance, so the linear Mathieu analysis fails when occupation grows.

name: Spin-orbit dynamics and chaotic tumbling
summary: Intermediate-axis instability and spin-orbit coupling give chaotic rotation of irregular moons such as Hyperion, and spin-orbit resonances like Mercury's 3:2.

name: Rigid rotation, free precession and pulsars
summary: Euler's equations for torque-free bodies describe free precession of neutron stars, and rotational dynamics governs pulsar spin-down and glitches, though the superfluid interior complicates a rigid-body model.
breaks: Neutron stars have superfluid interiors and elastic crusts, so a single rigid body fails.

name: Axial precession and obliquity climate cycles
summary: Torque-driven precession and obliquity variations (Milankovitch cycles) modulate insolation; obliquity stability, enforced by a large moon, affects habitability.

name: VLBI and EHT as van Cittert–Zernike imaging
summary: Radio interferometry measures visibilities that are Fourier components of source brightness, per van Cittert–Zernike; the EHT imaged the M87 and Sgr A* shadows from sparse coverage.

name: Interferometry and direct imaging of exoplanets
summary: Van Cittert–Zernike coherence underlies interferometric imaging and nulling, while coronagraphs use diffraction control and apodization to suppress starlight for direct imaging.

name: Hanbury Brown–Twiss stellar intensity interferometry
summary: Intensity correlations measured by Hanbury Brown and Twiss gave stellar angular diameters, founding photon-statistics optics and being revived with Cherenkov telescope arrays.

name: Diffraction limit and adaptive optics at the Galactic Centre
summary: Telescope resolution is set by the diffraction limit, and adaptive optics corrects atmospheric phase errors to track stellar orbits around Sgr A*.

name: Lensing as geometric optics in curved spacetime
summary: Light follows null geodesics, equivalent to rays in a medium with effective refractive index n = 1 − 2Φ/c²; the lens equation and Fermat's principle mirror thin-lens optics.
breaks: Lenses have no focal point (the deflection is not linear in impact parameter), and the lens is an extended mass whose profile fixes the images; strong-field lensing leaves the geometric-optics limit.

name: Telescope optics and survey instruments
summary: Aberration theory and wide-field optical design set the imaging performance of survey telescopes like ZTF and Rubin used for transient discovery.

name: Wave optics of lensing and fringes
summary: Lensing of coherent waves (FRBs, gravitational waves) shows interference between images, and diffraction from point lenses gives fringes when wavelength approaches the Schwarzschild radius, as in Fresnel optics.
breaks: Geometric optics is recovered only for w much greater than 1; strong dependence on lens profile and no analogue of aberration-free focusing.

name: Stokes parameters and E/B polarization
summary: CMB polarization is described with Stokes Q and U, decomposed into curl-free E and divergence-free B modes, a spin-2 field analogous to optical polarization states.

name: Faraday rotation and polarimetry of jets
summary: Birefringence of magnetized plasma rotates linear polarization as λ², letting radio polarimetry measure magnetic fields in jets, the Galaxy and intergalactic gas.

name: FRB dispersion and Faraday rotation as plasma probes
summary: Plasma refractive index gives frequency-dependent delay (dispersion measure) and Faraday rotation, which together weigh intergalactic baryons and magnetic fields along FRB sightlines.

name: Wave propagation in cold plasma
summary: The cold-plasma dispersion relation of EM waves, with cutoff at the plasma frequency, gives FRB pulse delay and scattering broadening by turbulent plasma.

name: Solar magnetic fields and MHD
summary: Maxwell's equations with induction and Ampère's law in the low-frequency limit give magnetohydrodynamics for solar fields, flux freezing and reconnection driving flares.
breaks: Displacement current is dropped and ideal conductivity assumed; reconnection requires non-ideal terms.

name: Relativistic beaming and Doppler boosting
summary: Lorentz transformations of fields and radiation give aberration and Doppler boosting of jet emission, explaining superluminal motion and blazar brightness.

name: Laser frequency combs for radial velocity
summary: Laser frequency combs and microresonator Kerr combs give precise wavelength calibration for spectrographs, targeting cm/s radial-velocity precision needed for Earth-like planets.

name: Astrophysical masers and lasers
summary: Population inversion and stimulated emission occur naturally as masers in star-forming regions and evolved-star envelopes, with narrow bright lines used for distances and kinematics.
breaks: Masers lack an optical cavity and are single-pass amplifiers, with no mode selection or coherence like a laser.

name: Radiation processes power high-energy sources
summary: Synchrotron, bremsstrahlung and inverse-Compton emission from relativistic charges, derived from Liénard–Wiechert fields, underlie GRBs, AGN jets, cosmic-ray signatures and FRBs.

name: Air-Cherenkov detection of cosmic rays
summary: Cherenkov light from air showers triggered by cosmic rays and gamma rays is imaged by IACTs such as H.E.S.S. and CTA, reconstructing primary energy and direction.

name: Cherenkov light detects neutrinos
summary: IceCube and KM3NeT detect Cherenkov light from relativistic charged secondaries of neutrino interactions in ice and water, using the cos θ = 1/(nβ) cone to reconstruct direction.

name: Neutrino telescopes rely on the Cherenkov effect
summary: The Frank–Tamm photon yield and the refractive-index dispersion of ice and seawater set the light output and detector response of neutrino telescopes.

name: Pulsar spin-down as magnetic dipole radiation
summary: A rotating magnetic dipole radiates at the rotation frequency, giving the braking index n=3 and characteristic age estimates for pulsars.

name: Synchrotron emission from AGN jets
summary: Relativistic electrons spiraling in jet magnetic fields emit beamed synchrotron radiation, giving power-law spectra, high polarization and Doppler boosting in blazars.

name: Synchrotron afterglow and fireball emission
summary: GRB afterglows are synchrotron emission from shock-accelerated electrons in a decelerating relativistic blast wave, with broken power-law spectra whose breaks map to electron energy and magnetic field.

name: Pulsar and magnetar radiation
summary: Pulsar magnetic-dipole braking uses the dipole radiation formula, and coherent curvature and synchrotron emission from magnetospheric particles produce radio and gamma-ray pulses.

name: Synchrotron in supernova remnants
summary: Radio and X-ray synchrotron emission from electrons accelerated at remnant shocks reveals magnetic field amplification and particle acceleration, linking to cosmic-ray origin.

name: Photon–baryon tight coupling via Thomson
summary: Thomson scattering couples photons to baryons before recombination, producing the acoustic oscillations; the visibility function and Silk damping follow from the scattering mean free path.

name: Thomson scattering polarizes the CMB
summary: Thomson scattering of anisotropic radiation by free electrons, with its dipole angular dependence, generates CMB linear polarization (E modes) at recombination and reionization.

name: Eddington limit and Compton coronae in AGN
summary: Thomson-limited radiation pressure caps accretion luminosity, and Comptonization of disk photons in hot coronae produces AGN X-ray power-law spectra.

name: Sunyaev–Zel'dovich inverse-Compton scattering
summary: CMB photons Compton-scattered by hot intracluster electrons gain energy, distorting the blackbody spectrum; the Kompaneets treatment of Compton scattering yields the thermal SZ signal used to find clusters.

name: Inverse Compton and synchrotron cooling of cosmic rays
summary: Relativistic electrons lose energy by synchrotron and inverse-Compton scattering on CMB and starlight, steepening spectra and producing TeV gamma rays, which limits the lifetime of cosmic-ray electrons.

name: Compton scattering in relativistic outflows
summary: Inverse-Compton and Thomson scattering set photospheric opacity and high-energy afterglow components in GRB fireballs; the Thomson optical depth fixes the compactness constraint on Lorentz factors.

name: Rayleigh and Mie scattering in exoplanet hazes
summary: Rayleigh slopes and Mie scattering by clouds and hazes shape transmission spectra, muting molecular features and giving blue-slope signatures, as for Earth's blue sky.

name: Electron-scattering opacity and Eddington limit
summary: Thomson scattering opacity sets radiation pressure in stellar interiors and the Eddington luminosity limiting massive stars and accretion.

name: First law in a comoving volume gives the fluid equation
summary: Applying dU=−p dV adiabatically to a comoving volume gives the cosmological continuity equation, so each component's equation of state w=p/ρ fixes ρ∝a^{-3(1+w)}. A cosmological constant (w=−1) keeps its density fixed as the volume grows; its negative pressure balances the energy books.
